title: Min and Max Distance Between Critical Points
description:
A critical point in a singly linked list is a node that is either a **local maximum** (`prev.val < curr.val > next.val`) or a **local minimum** (`prev.val > curr.val < next.val`). The first and last nodes cannot be critical points because they lack both neighbors.

Given the `head` of a linked list, return an integer array of length 2 `[minDistance, maxDistance]` representing the minimum and maximum distances (difference in node positions) between any two distinct critical points. If there are fewer than two critical points, return `[-1, -1]`.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [2, 10^4].
hints: Slide three consecutive pointers (`prev`, `curr`, `curr.next`) across the list in a single pass while tracking the current index.
The maximum distance is always between the first and last critical points; the minimum distance is the smallest gap between any two consecutive critical points.

examples.explanation: The list [3, 1] has no interior nodes, hence 0 critical points and [-1, -1].
Critical points are at indices 2 (val 1), 4 (val 5), and 5 (val 1), giving min distance 5-4=1 and max distance 5-2=3.
Critical points are at indices 1 (val 3) and 4 (val 3), so both min and max distance are 4-1=3.
